title: English Vocabulary 3 · Units 19–20
description: Reviewed B2 art, literary criticism, painting, theatre and film vocabulary, including arts collocations, word families and usage contrasts.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study using the user-provided book. Themes and learning targets were checked against the source; definitions, English examples and Brazilian Portuguese translations were newly authored.

audit.scope: Unit 19 and 20 study pages, arts diagram, artist photographs and art exercise illustrations, text and marginal notes, exercises 19.1–19.4 and 20.1–20.5, and answer-key entries.
audit.pronunciation: Conservative broad British IPA supplied for individual targets where reliable; phrase IPA omitted rather than inventing connected-speech patterns.
audit.languagePolicy: English throughout except natural Brazilian Portuguese translations in pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Consulted original textbook pages including visuals, exercises and answer keys; checked provenance, unique identifiers, item structure, speech targets and examples. No direct app/browser test.
audit.limitations: No bundled recordings. Browser import, TTS playback and speech recognition were not tested.

units.title: Unit 19 — Art and literature
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 19. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: The arts: art forms, artists, painting styles and literary criticism
learningObjectives: Distinguish art, the arts, fine art and performing arts, and use arts and crafts and works of art correctly.
Identify artists and artistic techniques, including sculpture, pottery, portraits, landscapes and still lifes.
Describe novels using plot, character, setting, series, literary, bestseller and critic.
Discuss reviews, publication, ebooks, advance copies, extracts and chapters.

sectionsChecked: A: Art and the arts; diagram and expressions
B: Types of art and artists; images and descriptions

items.pt: as artes; atividades artísticas em geral
items.example: The city festival celebrates the arts through music, literature and theatre.
items.note: Plural term covering many creative fields; broader than art in the narrow sense of painting and sculpture.

items.example: The gallery offers free classes in art for beginners.
items.note: Uncountable when referring to fine art generally; contrast plural the arts.

items.pt: a arte de; a habilidade de
items.example: He has mastered the art of telling engaging stories.
items.note: Art can refer to a particular skill or creative technique, not only visual works.

items.example: She studied fine art before becoming a professional sculptor.
items.note: Usually visual creative arts such as painting and sculpture; fine arts is also common as a plural category.

items.example: The college has a department of performing arts.
items.note: Arts presented to an audience, including drama, dance and music.

items.example: Her interest in literature began when she discovered short stories.
items.note: Books and other writing regarded as works of art.

items.example: I borrowed a biography of a pioneering scientist.
items.note: An account of somebody's life written by another person; compare autobiography.

items.pt: romance; livro de ficção em prosa
items.example: Her first novel is about two families living in different countries.
items.note: A substantial work of fiction; a short story is much shorter.

items.example: The magazine publishes a short story by a new writer every month.
items.note: A short piece of fictional prose, unlike a full-length novel.

items.example: The students discussed poetry from several different centuries.
items.note: Poetry is normally uncountable; an individual composition is a poem.

items.example: The school offers courses in drama and creative writing.
items.note: Here drama is acting and plays as an art form, not simply a difficult situation.

items.example: She developed an interest in theatre while at university.
items.note: British spelling theatre; refers to the art form or a place for stage performances.

items.example: Contemporary dance is a popular choice at the arts centre.
items.note: The art form or activity, not necessarily a particular event.

items.example: He is interested in cinema from across Europe.
items.note: Can refer to film as an art form or to a place where films are shown.

items.example: She enjoys ballet but prefers contemporary performances.
items.note: A type of theatrical dance; can denote the art form or a particular ballet.

items.example: The arts festival includes opera as well as theatre.
items.note: A form of musical drama with singers and instrumental accompaniment.

items.example: We went to a concert featuring a local orchestra.
items.note: A public performance of music, often part of the performing arts.

items.example: The radio station broadcasts classical music every evening.
items.note: A type of music rather than an individual concert.

items.example: The programme explored the history of rock music.
items.note: A category of popular music mentioned in the unit's arts diagram.

items.example: The festival included a concert of country and western music.
items.note: A music style; country music is a common shorter name.

items.example: She wants to study sculpture at art school.
items.note: Can mean the art of making three-dimensional works or a particular work.

items.example: Painting became his favourite artistic activity.
items.note: The activity or art; a painting is also a picture made with paint.

items.example: The old railway station is famous for its architecture.
items.note: Design of buildings and the artistic field of designing them.

items.pt: cerâmica; arte de produzir objetos de cerâmica
items.example: The exhibition includes handmade ceramics from several artists.
items.note: Objects made from clay and hardened by heat, or the art of making them.

items.example: She reads the arts page to find reviews of new exhibitions.
items.note: Section of a newspaper covering creative arts rather than general news.

items.pt: apreciador de arte; amante das artes
items.example: As an art lover, he visits local galleries whenever he travels.
items.note: Someone interested in and enthusiastic about works of art.

items.example: Her artistic skills helped her design the exhibition.
items.note: Describes skill, imagination or qualities connected with art; related to artist.

items.example: The museum has acquired an important work of art.
items.note: Plural is works of art, not work of arts; typically an individual artistic object.

items.example: The community centre runs an arts and crafts workshop on Saturdays.
items.note: Fixed plural phrase for making decorative or useful objects by hand.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The sculptor created a life-sized figure in stone.
items.note: A person who makes sculptures; do not confuse the person with sculpture.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: A bronze statue stands outside the library.
items.note: A three-dimensional representation of a person or animal, often made by a sculptor.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The artist was commissioned to create a statue for the city square.
items.note: A natural verb and noun combination for producing this kind of sculpture.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The potter sells handmade bowls and vases.
items.note: A craftsperson who makes objects from clay; contrast pottery, the product or craft.

items.pt: moldar um pote na roda de oleiro
items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The potter demonstrated how to throw a pot on a wheel.
items.note: Specialised ceramics expression: throw means shape wet clay on a rotating wheel.

items.pt: cerâmica; objetos de barro; ofício do ceramista
items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: Her pottery combines simple shapes with bright colours.
items.note: Uncountable for the craft or ceramic objects as a group; a potter is the maker.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: An architect drew up the plans for the new library.
items.note: Person who designs buildings; architecture is the field or style.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: She was asked to design a building for community events.
items.note: Design means plan its form and features, not necessarily construct it.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The gallery displayed an abstract painting made up of bold shapes.
items.note: Abstract art does not attempt to represent real objects in a realistic way.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The artist painted a portrait of her grandmother.
items.note: A depiction of a person; a portrait need not be a photograph.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: He painted a landscape showing hills and a river.
items.note: In art, a picture of outdoor scenery; landscape can also mean the actual surroundings.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The students arranged fruit and flowers for a still life.
items.note: Artistic representation of objects that do not move; plural still lifes.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The original painting is kept in a private collection.
items.note: Made by the original artist, rather than being a copy or reproduction.

items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: She bought a copy of the portrait for her office.
items.note: A copy is not the original artwork, even when visually similar.

items.pt: reprodução; cópia de uma obra de arte
items.section: B · Types of art and artists
items.example: The gift shop sells reproductions of famous paintings.
items.note: A version made from an existing artwork; compare original.

items.pt: romancista; autor ou autora de romances
items.example: The novelist won an award for her latest book.
items.note: Someone who writes novels; related to novel, not simply any author.

items.example: The detective series follows the same investigator across six books.
items.note: Series has the same form in singular and plural; it often reuses characters.

items.pt: romance romântico; livro de ficção romântica
items.example: Her romantic novels focus on relationships across generations.
items.note: Romantic describes a love-related story; do not confuse with novel meaning new in other contexts.

items.pt: ambientação histórica; contexto histórico de uma narrativa
items.example: The story has a historical setting in nineteenth-century London.
items.note: Setting is the time and place of the events, not the plot itself.

items.pt: livro de grande sucesso de vendas; best-seller
items.example: The author's debut became a bestseller within weeks.
items.note: A book that sells in very large numbers; not necessarily a critical success.

items.example: A respected critic praised the novel's dialogue.
items.note: A person who publishes evaluations of works, not simply someone who dislikes them.

items.example: The plot becomes more complex in the final chapters.
items.note: Sequence of events in a story; not interchangeable with characters or setting.

items.example: The ending felt predictable after the first few chapters.
items.note: Easy to guess in advance; often negative when commenting on a plot.

items.example: The main character makes a difficult decision early in the story.
items.note: A person in a fictional work, not necessarily an actor.

items.example: The characters' reactions felt realistic to the readers.
items.note: Believable and similar to real life; compare abstract for a type of visual art.

items.example: The journal publishes essays on literary fiction.
items.note: Can suggest serious artistic writing rather than fiction aimed mainly at popularity.

items.example: Her review of the novel appeared in the Sunday newspaper.
items.note: An evaluation of a book, film or other work; a critic may write it.

items.example: The publisher delayed publication until September.
items.note: The process or event of making a work available; also the printed item itself.

items.example: She downloaded the ebook to read during her journey.
items.note: Electronic book, often downloaded or accessed through an app.

items.pt: exemplar antecipado; cópia enviada antes do lançamento
items.example: Reviewers received an advance copy of the novel several weeks early.
items.note: A copy made available before the official publication date.

items.example: The opening passage introduces the story's setting.
items.note: A short continuous part of text at the beginning of a work.

items.example: The publisher posted a short extract from the new book.
items.note: A selected section of a longer work; unlike a review, it is part of the work itself.

items.example: The second chapter reveals why the family left home.
items.note: A major numbered division of a book or narrative.

items.example: A poem does not always have to rhyme to be effective.
items.note: As a verb, rhyme describes words ending with the same sound; poetry need not rhyme.

items.example: The artist used oil paints for a large landscape.
items.note: The exercise contrasts oil-based painting with watercolour painting.

items.example: She uses watercolours to create delicate pictures of plants.
items.note: British English spelling watercolours; can mean paints or paintings made with them.

units.title: Unit 20 — Theatre and cinema
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 20. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Stage and screen: performances, casts, film-making and arts events
learningObjectives: Describe theatre productions using set, costume, cast, direction, performance and rave reviews.
Choose audience versus viewer, and use cinema, ballet, theatre and opera with appropriate articles.
Discuss films using opening scene, be set in, capture, dialogue, script, screenplay and score.
Ask about arts events, stages and venues, and use promote, appear in and appearance in context.

sectionsChecked: A: At the theatre; Language help about articles
B: At the cinema; dialogue and definitions
C: Other words connected with events in the arts

items.example: The theatre is preparing a new production of a classic play.
items.note: A particular staged version of a play, organised by a director and performers.

items.example: The designer created a simple set for the first act.
items.note: Stage scenery, furniture and structures; often plural sets for multiple scenes.

items.example: The costumes helped establish the period in which the play takes place.
items.note: Clothes worn by actors or performers, distinct from the scenery.

items.example: The cast includes performers from several different countries.
items.note: The group of actors in a production; compare audience, the people watching.

items.pt: direção artística; direção de uma peça
items.example: The play succeeded partly because of its thoughtful direction.
items.note: The way a director organises a production; not travel directions.

items.example: Her final performance was both moving and convincing.
items.note: One instance of acting or performing; a show can contain multiple performances.

items.example: The lead actor gave a memorable performance in the final scene.
items.note: Common collocation: give a good, powerful or excellent performance.

items.example: The new production got rave reviews from theatre critics.
items.note: Get rave reviews means receive highly enthusiastic published evaluations.

items.example: The comedy received rave reviews after its opening night.
items.note: Rave here means very enthusiastic, not criticism in general.

items.example: She trained in modern dance before joining the company.
items.note: In the unit, dance often refers to modern artistic dance; compare ballet.

items.example: Their company combines traditional techniques with modern ballet.
items.note: Ballet may be traditional or modern; modern ballet is not the same term as modern dance.

items.example: The comedian entertained the audience with stories about everyday life.
items.note: A person who makes people laugh; not the same as a comedy, a humorous work.

items.example: The performers entertained the children with music and stories.
items.note: Verb meaning provide enjoyable amusement or interest; entertainer is a related noun.

items.pt: artista de entretenimento; profissional que diverte o público
items.example: The entertainer performs at festivals throughout the summer.
items.note: A person whose work is to entertain an audience.

items.example: The show begins at half past seven.
items.note: An entertainment event, possibly featuring different performers.

items.example: The audience applauded when the actors returned to the stage.
items.note: People watching or listening to a performance; contrast TV viewers.

items.pt: telespectador; pessoa que assiste à televisão
items.example: Many viewers watched the interview at home.
items.note: In the unit, viewer means someone watching a TV programme, not a theatre audience member.

items.example: She is interested in opera but rarely attends live performances.
items.note: When speaking generally about this art form, the article is often omitted; compare the opera for a particular visit or performance.

items.pt: a ópera; uma ida à ópera
items.example: We are going to the opera on Saturday night.
items.note: The + opera commonly refers to an outing to a specific performance.

items.pt: o teatro; uma ida ao teatro
items.example: Would you like to come to the theatre with us tomorrow?
items.note: For attendance at a particular event, the theatre is a normal British English expression.

items.pt: o cinema; uma ida ao cinema
items.example: They went to the cinema to watch a new film.
items.note: The cinema often refers to a place or outing; cinema without the can refer to film as art.

items.example: The local cinema is showing a documentary this weekend.
items.note: A cinema shows a film; showing can be used in announcements of screenings.

items.pt: estar a fim de ir; ter vontade de ir
items.example: Do you fancy going to the cinema after work?
items.note: Informal British English: fancy + -ing, not fancy to go.

items.example: The opening scene takes place at a crowded railway station.
items.note: A scene is one part of a film or play, often in a single location.

items.example: The film is set in a small coastal town.
items.note: Be set in + place or time describes a story's setting.

items.pt: locação; local onde se passa ou se filma uma cena
items.example: The film used several locations in the Scottish Highlands.
items.note: Place used for filming or represented as part of the story.

items.example: The film captures the uncertainty of starting a new life.
items.note: Here capture means represent a feeling or quality convincingly, not physically seize it.

items.example: The actors rehearsed using an early version of the script.
items.note: Words for a play or film; compare screenplay, a film-specific script with instructions.

items.example: The dialogue sounds natural despite the unusual setting.
items.note: Speech exchanged by characters, whether in films, plays or books; normally uncountable in this use.

items.example: The director worked closely with the actors during filming.
items.note: Person responsible for organising the creative making of a play or film; direction names the work.

items.example: The screenplay includes directions for the actors and camera crew.
items.note: A text written specifically for a film; contains dialogue and other instructions.

items.pt: trilha musical original; música de um filme
items.example: The composer wrote a moving score for the drama.
items.note: Here score is the music composed for a film, not a sports result.

items.pt: diálogo de um filme; falas de personagens
items.example: The film dialogue was particularly sharp and funny.
items.note: Dialogue is the conversational language in a film, not its background score.

items.pt: trilha sonora original; música composta para um filme
items.example: The film score creates tension without distracting from the story.
items.note: Music written for the film; not necessarily every commercial song used in it.

items.pt: realizar uma apresentação; encenar um espetáculo
items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The drama group put on a performance for local families.
items.note: A performing group puts on a performance, play or show; related to do a performance.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: A large curtain separated the audience from the stage.
items.note: Area where performers appear, as distinct from the set or the venue.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The new theatre has a versatile stage that suits different productions.
items.note: Able to serve several purposes or adapt to different uses.

items.pt: o que está em cartaz; qual é a programação
items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: What's on at the theatre this weekend?
items.note: Ask What's on at a cinema or theatre; on describes scheduled entertainment.

items.pt: local de evento; espaço para apresentações
items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The organisers booked a larger venue for the concert.
items.note: A place where an event is held, such as a hall or theatre.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The actors appeared on the radio to promote their new play.
items.note: To give publicity to a show or product; promotion is the noun.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The theatre planned an online promotion for the opening week.
items.note: In this context, publicity or marketing, not promotion to a higher job position.

items.pt: atuar em; participar de uma obra artística
items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: She will appear in a new comedy next month.
items.note: Appear in a film, play or show means perform as part of its cast.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The actor makes a brief appearance near the end of the film.
items.note: Noun related to appear; not physical appearance in this context.

items.section: C · Other words connected with events in the arts
items.example: The production used a revolving stage to change the scenery quickly.
items.note: Exercise 20.3 describes a stage that can rotate to reveal different sets.

items.example: The theatre's new comedy made everyone laugh.
items.note: The work or genre, in contrast with comedian, the person.

items.example: She prefers romantic comedies to action films.
items.note: A film or play centred on romantic relationships with a humorous treatment.

items.pt: frequentador de concertos ou shows musicais
items.example: He is a keen concert-goer and attends live music events regularly.
items.note: A person who goes to concerts; mentioned in the open-ended exercise.
